newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss cabinet blocks Mobutu assets.
newsitem.headline: Swiss cabinet blocks Mobutu assets.

text.p: The Swiss Federal Council (cabinet) on Saturday blocked all assets that ousted Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and his family may have in Switzerland, an official statement said.
The joint statement issued in Berne by the Foreign Ministry and Finance Ministry said the move took effect immediately and would stay in effect for a year.

The freezing of Mobutu and his family's possible holdings in Switzerland -- or those administered from the country -- comes a day after Swiss federal judicial and police authorities froze his luxury villa at Savigny, above Lausanne. The 30-room villa is worth about $5.5 million.
Swiss media have speculated that Mobutu may have some $4.5 billion in assets stashed in the Alpine country.

"The Federal Council today (Saturday) adopted a decree blocking the assets of the Mobutu family in Switzerland, as a provisional measure," the statement said. "Under the terms of the decree, the blocking of the assets of Mr. Mobutu and the members of his family takes effect immediately and concerns wealth in Switzerland or that administered from Switzerland."

Matthias Kraaft, a federal government spokesman, told Swiss Television: "It means that anyone handling funds belonging to the Mobutu family may not transfer them and anyone holding such funds must announce them to the Finance Ministry." Asked whether this meant there were funds, he said: "We don't know."
